explain.say: See the first dot, a cave painting? In Sulawesi, Indonesia, someone painted human-like figures with a pig over 51,000 years ago. Before writing, most stories lived only in people's voices, passed from mouth to mouth. Why do you think they painted it on a wall?

explain.say: See the printing press, around 1450? Johannes Gutenberg's press in Germany made books much cheaper and faster to make, so far more people could own stories. Printing had begun even earlier in China and Korea. Then in 1895, the Lumière brothers showed films in Paris. How would it feel to see a moving picture for the first time?

faq.q: What is the oldest story in the world?
faq.a: The oldest known story in pictures may be a cave painting in Sulawesi, Indonesia, at least 51,200 years old. The oldest written stories include poems about Gilgamesh from Mesopotamia, from around 2100 BCE.

faq.q: What does the Sulawesi cave painting show?
faq.a: It shows three human-like figures around a wild pig, which researchers see as a scene, an early kind of story. It was dated in 2024 to at least 51,200 years old.
asks: What is the oldest cave art?

faq.q: What is the Epic of Gilgamesh?
faq.a: It is one of the oldest written stories, from Mesopotamia in today's Iraq. It tells of King Gilgamesh of Uruk, his friend Enkidu and his search to live forever. The earliest poems date from around 2100 BCE.

faq.q: How did the printing press change storytelling?
faq.a: Gutenberg's press, from around 1450 in Germany, let books be copied quickly and cheaply, so many more people could read stories and ideas. Earlier, block printing and movable type had been invented in China and Korea.

faq.q: How do we tell stories today?
faq.a: Today stories reach us through books, films, TV, games, podcasts and streaming apps on phones, often shared instantly around the world. People also still tell stories face to face.

facts: The Leang Karampuang cave painting in Sulawesi was dated in 2024 to at least 51,200 years ago.
Bi Sheng invented movable type in China around 1040 CE, and Korea's Jikji (1377) is the oldest surviving book printed with movable metal type.
The Lumière brothers held one of the first public film screenings in Paris on 28 December 1895.

quiz.why: The cave painting is over 51,000 years old, far older than printing (about 1450) or films (1895).

wrong.0: Gutenberg's press is only about 575 years old.

quiz.say: What did the printing press change?
quiz.why: Printing let many copies be made quickly, so more people could own books.

wrong.1: It made far more books, not fewer.
wrong.2: It spread books to many more ordinary people.
